title: priority-bucketed-kv-lease-and-cooldown-fidelity-ladder-for-oom-recovery
creator: Aisha Thompson
description:
Summary:
We are seeing transient OOMs during high-concurrency continuous-batching workloads where long-lived KV entries plus bursty request patterns push GPU memory usage beyond headroom. This ticket implements a coordinated mitigation: priority-bucketed KV leases (time-limited reservations), a cooldown-based admission controller for burst windows, and a fidelity ladder that progressively reduces memory footprint before triggering a hard model fallback. Goal is to avoid hard OOMs, preserve best-effort latency for high-priority requests, and provide deterministic retries and rollout hooks for fallback models.

Proposed design:
1) KV lease buckets: requests are assigned a priority bucket (P0/P1/P2) at admission. Each bucket has a configurable KV lease quota (bytes and entry count) per GPU instance. Leases expire after short TTLs (configurable e.g., 30s) and are renewed on access.
2) Cooldown admission controller: when a GPU crosses a soft-headroom threshold (e.g., 88% memory), the controller activates a cooldown window for the offending allocation cohort. New low-priority requests are admitted with degraded guarantees (shorter leases, no KV prefetch). Cooldown decays exponentially if pressure reduces.
3) Fidelity ladder: rather than binary fallback, implement fractional fidelity steps per request path: token-shedding, KV weak-references (allow stale KV reuse), attention-sparsity hints, then switch to a lighter quantized model variant or micro-model. Each step reduces memory cost and is reversible when headroom restores.
4) Deterministic retry policy: requests that hit a graceful-degrade step receive a deterministic retry token allowing them to re-enter the queue with relaxed latency SLOs and higher chance of cache hits. Retries are rate-limited to prevent cascading pressure.
5) Observability & rollout: add a per-instance telemetry stream for lease usage by bucket, cooldown events, fidelity-step transitions, and OOM near-misses. Expose metrics to Console for per-model dashboards and alarm thresholds.

API/Config changes:
- New admission config: {"buckets": [{"name":"P0","kv_quota_mb":""},{"name":"P1"}], "cooldown_threshold_pct": "", "fidelity_steps_order": ""} (represented in Console as fields; backend accepts JSON blob).
- Hook points for model variants: model catalog entries gain optional lightweight_variant and micro_model fields.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit + integration tests for lease accounting and TTL renewal semantics.
- Simulated load test reproducing previous OOM signature must now show no hard OOMs and <=10% degraded responses (fidelity-step applied) under same load.
- Metric plumbing: per-GPU lease usage, cooldown_active boolean, fidelity_step histogram available in Console.
- A/B rollout to 10% of serving fleet with automatic rollback on >3x increase in client error-rate.

Trade-offs & notes:
- Additional bookkeeping (leases) increases CPU/metadata memory; bucket granularity should be kept small to bound overhead.
- TTLs need balance: too short causes thrash/extra prefetch; too long reduces effectiveness. We will test 10s/30s/60s in staging.
- This design prefers graceful quality degradation over immediate model fallback to preserve latency for critical paths.

Next steps:
- Implement lease bookkeeping module + TTL sweeper (ENG pair: Marco + Liwei)
- Add cooldown admission hook to batch admission service (ENG: Shreya)
- Implement fidelity-step adapters in runtime (quantized path already present; wire micro-model switching)
- Create staging load test harness and dashboards (SRE + Console)

Links to artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUN/priority-bucketed-kv-lease
- Load test harness + scripts: https://github.com/redwood-inference/oom-tests/tree/priority-leases

2026-03-11 - Marco Rivera: Spike completed for KV lease accounting. Prototype keeps per-GPU map of bucket->bytes and entry_count. Observed metadata overhead ~1.2MB per 100k leases. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/9182
2026-03-11 - Liwei Zhang: Implemented TTL sweeper; found corner-case where renewals race eviction. Proposed lock-free renewal token to avoid blocking admission threads.

2026-03-12 - Shreya Patel: Integrated cooldown hook into batching admission. In local sim, cooldown reduced OOM near-misses by 70% but increased 95p latency for P2 by ~12ms. Investigating rate limiting window size.

qa_notes: Run staging harness with three settings: TTL=10s/30s/60s across 3 seed workloads. Verify zero hard OOMs and measure degraded-response-rate. Document rollback criteria in runbook.
implementation_notes: Keep bucket metadata compact; use 16-bit counters where possible; lease bytes tracked in 32-bit. Add feature flag runtime.priority_kv_leases to gate rollout.
